theme.title: Detroit defense
theme.subtitle: Pistons, 1989 and 2004
theme.recap: Detroit won with defense twice: the Bad Boys of 1989 and the 2004 team that held five straight opponents under 70.

questions.prompt: How many games did the 1988–89 "Bad Boys" Pistons win?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: finishing in first place in the Central Division with a league-best 63–19 record

funFacts.text: That season marked the Bad Boys' first in the brand-new Palace of Auburn Hills.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: moved from the Pontiac Silverdome to their brand-new arena known as The Palace of Auburn Hills

funFacts.text: Detroit traded Adrian Dantley to Dallas midseason for Mark Aguirre, a longtime friend of Isiah Thomas.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: traded Dantley to the Dallas Mavericks in exchange for All-Star forward Mark Aguirre

funFacts.text: Detroit opened its regular season with eight consecutive wins — an early sign of the championship run to come.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Pistons got off to a fast start by winning their first eight games of the regular season.

questions.prompt: In Game 3 of the 1989 Finals, Joe Dumars scored how many points in a row in the third quarter?
questions.context: 1989 NBA Finals · Game 3 · at Los Angeles
questions.note: 17 in a row, on his way to 31.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Joe Dumars scored 31 points, scoring 17 consecutive points in the third quarter

funFacts.text: Magic Johnson left the third Finals game after only a few minutes because of injury.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Magic Johnson missed most of Game 3 due to injury, exiting after five minutes

funFacts.text: Dennis Rodman hauled in 19 rebounds in the game despite battling back spasms.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Dennis Rodman, despite having back spasms, had 19 rebounds

funFacts.text: The Pistons had swept both Boston and Milwaukee before battling Michael Jordan's Bulls.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: sweeping both the Boston Celtics and the Milwaukee Bucks

questions.prompt: Joe Dumars was 1989 Finals MVP. What was his scoring average in the series?
questions.context: 1989 NBA Finals · four games vs Lakers

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Dumars was named Finals MVP after averaging 27.3 points per game during the series

funFacts.text: Detroit's Finals victory was the first NBA title in the history of the franchise.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: capturing their first NBA championship

funFacts.text: Kareem Abdul-Jabbar retired after the series, ending a remarkable 20-season NBA career.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Kareem Abdul-Jabbar announced his retirement from the NBA at age 42 at the end of his 20th season

funFacts.text: The team embraced the 'Bad Boys' label as both an identity and an advertising theme.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the team, led by Isiah Thomas and Bill Laimbeer, had embraced the title as a marketing brand

questions.prompt: The 2003–04 Pistons were the first team to hold how many straight opponents under 70 points?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
